description: How a row filter's field is found on a row whose keys may be bare or qualified with an object name. Exists because the lookup fell back to the field-name matcher, which drops qualifiers, so a filter on 'patients.region' could read 'encounters.region'. A bare filter matching several qualified keys used whichever came first (issue #32).
notes: Lookup order, identical in every SDK: (1) an exact key is used as-is. (2) Otherwise every key the field-name matcher accepts is a candidate, EXCEPT a key whose object qualifier conflicts with the filter's. Both must be qualified and the qualifiers (everything before the last '.') must differ, compared ASCII case-insensitively (only A-Z folds to a-z). A qualified filter may still read a bare key, and a bare filter may read a qualified key. (3) Exactly one candidate supplies the value. None, or more than one, is MISSING, and a MISSING field drops the row for every operator (spec section 7). Each case carries its own records because key ORDER is part of what is being tested; the runners must preserve the order the fixture writes. Each case carries a full policy so the shared corpus walk validates it against policy-definition.schema.json.

cases.name: qualified-filter-ignores-other-object-key-equals
cases.notes: The reported defect. 'patients.region' must not be read from 'encounters.region' just because the leaf names coincide; with no candidate the field is MISSING and the row is dropped.

cases.name: qualified-filter-ignores-other-object-key-notEquals
cases.notes: MISSING drops the row for the negative operators too. Reading the other object's value would keep the row ('eu' != 'us').

cases.name: qualified-filter-ignores-other-object-key-notIn
cases.notes: As notEquals: an absent field is not 'not in the list'.

cases.name: qualified-filter-ignores-other-object-key-isNull
cases.notes: Another object's present-and-null column must not satisfy isNull for this object: the field is absent, not null.

cases.name: qualified-filter-ignores-other-object-key-isNotNull
cases.notes: Another object's present value must not satisfy isNotNull for this object.

cases.name: qualified-filter-ignores-other-object-key-with-extra-qualifier
cases.notes: The key's qualifier ('db.encounters') differs from the filter's ('patients'), so it is not a candidate even though the matcher alone would accept it on the leaf.

cases.name: qualified-filter-picks-own-object-conflicting-key-first
cases.notes: No exact key (the filter's case differs), so lookup falls to the matcher. The conflicting 'ENCOUNTERS.REGION' key comes first and must be skipped; 'PATIENTS.REGION' is the only candidate.

cases.name: qualified-filter-picks-own-object-conflicting-key-last
cases.notes: The same as the previous case with the key order reversed. The answer must not depend on key order.

cases.name: qualified-filter-picks-bare-key-over-conflicting-key-conflicting-first
cases.notes: A bare 'region' key is a candidate for 'patients.region'; 'encounters.region' is not. So 'region' is the only candidate whatever the order.

cases.name: qualified-filter-picks-bare-key-over-conflicting-key-conflicting-last
cases.notes: The same as the previous case with the key order reversed.

cases.name: qualified-filter-matches-bare-key
cases.notes: Rows the tool has already projected carry bare keys. A qualified filter still reads them.

cases.name: bare-filter-matches-single-qualified-key
cases.notes: A bare filter reads a qualified key when that key is the only candidate.

cases.name: bare-filter-ambiguous-across-objects-equals
cases.notes: 'region' matches both 'patients.region' and 'encounters.region'. That is ambiguous, so the field is MISSING and every row is dropped, in either key order and even when the two values agree.

cases.name: bare-filter-ambiguous-across-objects-notEquals
cases.notes: Ambiguity fails closed for the negative operators too. Picking either key would keep at least one of these rows.

cases.name: bare-filter-ambiguous-across-objects-isNull
cases.notes: An ambiguous field does not satisfy isNull, even when one of the candidates is null.

cases.name: bare-filter-ambiguous-across-objects-isNotNull
cases.notes: An ambiguous field does not satisfy isNotNull, even when both candidates are present.

cases.name: exact-qualified-key-wins-over-conflicting-key
cases.notes: An exact key is used as-is. The conflicting key comes first and is never consulted.

cases.name: exact-bare-key-wins-over-ambiguous-qualified-keys
cases.notes: A bare filter with an exact bare key present uses that key. The two qualified keys, which would be ambiguous on their own, are never consulted.

cases.name: exact-key-wins-over-case-variant-of-itself
cases.notes: The exact key 'patients.region' wins over its case variant 'PATIENTS.REGION'. Without the exact key the two would be ambiguous.

cases.name: qualifier-comparison-is-case-insensitive-for-a-match
cases.notes: 'Patients' and 'PATIENTS' are the same object: field-name matching is case-insensitive (spec section 4).

cases.name: qualifier-comparison-is-case-insensitive-for-a-conflict
cases.notes: A case difference does not turn a different object into the same one. 'Encounters' still conflicts with 'patients'.

cases.name: case-variant-keys-of-same-object-are-ambiguous
cases.notes: With no exact key, 'patients.region' and 'PATIENTS.REGION' are two candidates. More than one candidate is MISSING, even for the same object.

cases.name: qualified-filter-with-bare-and-own-qualified-key-is-ambiguous
cases.notes: With no exact key, the bare 'region' and the case-variant 'PATIENTS.REGION' are both candidates for 'patients.region', so the lookup is ambiguous and the row is dropped.

cases.name: qualified-filter-ignores-key-with-longer-qualifier-of-same-table
cases.notes: Qualifiers are compared whole. 'db.patients' is not 'patients', so a key 'db.patients.region' is not a candidate for the filter 'patients.region'. It is dropped, which fails closed; no suffix matching is attempted.

cases.name: longer-qualifier-filter-ignores-shorter-qualified-key
cases.notes: The reverse: the filter 'db.patients.region' does not read the key 'patients.region'.

cases.name: glob-filter-qualifier-is-literal-against-a-qualified-key
cases.notes: Glob characters in a row filter's qualifier are not expanded for the qualifier comparison. '*' is not 'patients', so the qualified key is not a candidate.

cases.name: glob-filter-still-reads-a-bare-key
cases.notes: A bare key has no qualifier to conflict with, so the filter '*.region' still reads 'region' through the field-name matcher.

cases.name: non-ascii-qualifier-folds-ascii-only-conflict
cases.notes: The qualifier comparison folds only A-Z to a-z. 'PATİENTS' (U+0130, capital I with dot above) folds to 'patİents', which is not 'pati̇ents' (i followed by U+0307, combining dot above). Full Unicode lower-casing would make them equal in some SDKs and not others, so the qualifiers conflict and the row is dropped.

cases.name: non-ascii-qualifier-folds-ascii-only-match
cases.notes: 'PATİENTS' and 'patİents' differ only in ASCII letters, so they fold to the same qualifier and the key is the one candidate.
